transcript.text: Okay, well, have got 07:00, so I will call the meeting to order. And the first item on the agenda after that is roll call and seating of alternates. I see Anne Cremay is present. Scott is here. Steve is here. I haven't seen Leanne yet. And so, at this point, I will seat Susan for Leanne. I am present and we also have Ann Blanchard who will not be seated tonight. Next item is addition or changes to the agenda and for the sake of completeness, I would like to add new business, item six, Charlie and Delta. Charlie being a referral under eight-twenty four of the Connecticut General Statutes improvement to property of the town of Andover located at 15 Center Street, former firehouse. And Delta being use of local open space funds as a match for the proposed acquisition of the Ladano property located on Shawty Mill Road. These two items were on the agenda that got sent out to all of the Commission members. However, as I looked online and on the calendar today, the version there did not have those two items.
I printed it out and it's here. Think it was added earlier this morning. Well, sometime this morning.

I looked 06:30 tonight and did not see the updated version on the website. So anyhow, just to avoid any miscommunication with anybody, I'll make a motion to add those two items. I'll second that. Thank you, Scott.

All in favor, raise your hand. Okay, and that's the motion passes unanimously 500. Item four, public speak. I don't think we've got anybody from the public here that's wanting to speak tonight. I think, Hank, your only interest is probably in the open space acquisition coming up later on. Hello, Leanne, is that you? Moving on to Item five, old business. The first item is update on proposed amendments to the signed regulations and that is just to remind everybody that those signed regulations will be brought to public hearing prior to our July meeting, and we will have the public hearing and possibly take action on those following the public hearing. The old business 5B update on the gravel operation 517 Route 6. Jim, do you have anything for us on that? Well, I did have a conversation with Chris Bell,

today as well as a few weeks back. No material is leaving the site and he plans to come in with a revised restoration plan and do the restoration hopefully in the fall, late summer, and seed it at such time as nominate the turtles to seed it in September when the seed's gonna take. We just wanna seed it prior to August. So we will see that. I don't wanna say August, but I don't want to say July, but believe it'll believe we will see it July. I did indicate to Ms. Hutchinson, who has property adjacent, that she would have an opportunity to review the plan prior to that meeting. I made Chris aware of that, that he needs to get it in in time to do that.

Okay. I know in last month's meeting minutes, it talked about Chris, Jim, and Hank going over to look at the gravel pit operation together. Did you guys get a chance to do that yet, Jim? Or is that being held in the bay and spending the deferral till July of the restoration plan?
I would like to do it with the with the plan in hand.

Yeah. Is that okay with you, Hank? Yeah, I agree. I've been on jet. I've been because the net that you know once once the turtle nesting season broke, I was down there pretty much most nights because I wanted to monitor to make sure that nobody was getting around the fence and into the active area and also to see what we were getting for turtle activity in the back conservation area. So I agree with Jim. I'd like to, you know, have the plan and then and then meet Chris in the field. There have been some persistent issues with integrity of the barrier fence that separates the

conservation area from the from the work area, where wind is primarily been causing it to pull up where it's not towed in. I sent an email out, I think was it yesterday, Jim, the day before, I can't remember now, to Chris sort of indicating that, you know, a part of a section needed to be fixed after that last windstorm that we had. But I haven't heard back from them. But the turtle activity is kind of slowed down in that area.

Okay. I guess a comment I would make to the Commission members, and I was wondering if we should do a sidewalk over on the gravel pit either before we discuss the restoration plan or maybe with, you know, Jim and Hank after we have a restoration plan or something to see how all this is going to wind up, or do we wait till the whole thing is done? Anybody have any thoughts on interest in a sidewalk?

I'll go. I think it would be a good idea, Jed, and it might also be a good idea to have a final plan for the restoration showing the elevations because we weren't sure how much more material was going to be removed before they did the restoration?

Yes, and that was certainly, you know, I think it would be good to see what's going on there have a fighting chance of making the best decision on the restoration plan. Do we think if we were to get the plan presented to us in July, Then we do a site plan or a site visit after the July meeting and vote on the restoration plan in August. Does that sound like a reasonable plan of approach?
I think that would work. I don't think that would. Okay,
so we'll do nothing else on the gravel pit at this point until we get the site plan and Chris can walk us through that. And Jim, I think that Chris promised us to have a spot out there with
that two ninety four elevation there also. Yep. So we could all see.
Yeah, it would be good to have Chris, you know, lead us around to

show us the plan after it's ready. I would also go remind Chris, Jim, that I was hoping to see a restoration plan that just had the final site, what the final site was going to look like and not have all the intermediate So, stuff in it's easier for us to take a look at understanding what we wanted to have there. Leanne, are you with us now? Yes. Okay. So, are you ready to join the commission? Yes.

Okay. So, at time 07:11, we will see Leanne Hutchinson and Susan England will go back to being an alternate. I also see that we have had somebody named Keith join us. Did you have any public comment for us before we go on down the road, Keith? Or were you here for a specific item on the agenda tonight? A specific item. Okay, very good. Keith is here for Rosewood Acres.

Am here to address that. It rang a bell as soon as as soon as I asked that question. I said, okay, I saw that name on some documents here. Moving on to old business 5C. Set public hearing for proposed amendment to Section 17 of the zoning regs alcohol establishment and changed the title to Alcohol Cannabis Establishments. I would like to make a motion that at our July public hearing, we also take public comment on Section 17 of our zoning regs. I forgot to make that part of the motion last time. Jim has set those regulations out to the other towns in Groggs for review, we've got that working. But as long as we were going to do the public hearing on the sign regs, I wanted to do the alcohol cannabis changes at the same time. So my motion is to add the changes to Section 17 of the zoning regulations to the July public hearing. I'll second that. Thanks, Steve.
Any discussion? Okay. All in favor, raise your hand. Leanne, I don't see you. You have to tell me yes or no. Yes.

Okay, thank you. So the motion passes five zero zero. Moving on to new business. And first up is the lot line revision of Rosewood Acres Subdivision. And so Jim, do you have any preliminary information on why

this is coming to the Zoning Commission? Sure, just for some background, if some of you were involved with this, others weren't, back years ago, I don't recall when, ten or fifteen years ago, there was a 10 lot subdivision at the corner of Route 6 and Route 87. There's also a little street in there, Lindholm Corners, which goes down in cul de sacs, off 87. Well, they're short lived on those three streets. There were eight residential lots, two commercial lots. It improved. No, it didn't require any municipal improvements. No lots got sold, no improvements were made, no driveways were installed. As it turned out, it's extremely difficult property to develop in accordance with that plan anyway. Long driveways, market conditions, have you. So the owner, Keith Grimaldi, who is present, approached me about combining the lots, sort of starting over. And initially, he talked about just combining it into a single lot. And and then there was some discussion later on about retaining the commercial lots. I was I didn't know how that would how to best handle it. I do I had gotten some guidance from Mark Brantz on a previous property that lot line revisions of or the avoidance of subdivisions does require commission action. This was a little it's kind of was a little different, and I did go back to him, and I I told him what was being proposed at this time, and he suggested that

first, he he said that there's nothing in the statutes that would specifically address this situation. Kind of throughout sort of a common sense approach, which was to bring the revised plan to the commission to be approved or deciding. Now, I'm not I mean, I had a conversation with mister Romali earlier today, and I think he's still trying to decide, what the best approach is to do as far as whether he wants to combine it into a single lot or retain those commercial lots. But what I what I'd like to suggest is that back with the commission's blessing, come back with a plan, showing what he'd really like to do, and I would in the interim come up with a draft letter of approval that would kind of address the conditions. And specifically, what I'm getting at is, I mean, there was open space requirements in the initial approval. Somehow, I think that they would have to be void, and there's a requirement that a cistern be installed fire protection. And that would have to be somehow at least clarified that it's no longer a condition of approval.

And I would take that proposed letter and also it off Mark. He owner, mister Camaldi, also had a concern about if it might impact a lot I'm sorry. Curb cut from DOT, curb cut approval. And I no way I could have answered that question today. So I mean, that would be something I'd have to address, kind of walk through the old conditions of approval and address each of them. And I can't say that would I mean, it would be up to Keith as to when he comes back. Mean, could say July, but I don't know whether he'd have a plan in place or have a plan drafted by then. And I believe he also wanted to speak to the commission, sort of get a feel for what the commission might like to see happen on
that lot. And that might drive his decision as to what his revised plan would show. Does that sound right to you? Mister Grimaldi, guess Oh, yes. I'm sorry.

Yes. That's what we discussed. Again, this is all new territory to go backwards like this. But since all the reg changes in the last few years are now making this more viable for regular development versus what was basically the only option back in 2010 to make long quarter mile driveways with eight acre lots and so on and so on. Obviously that never became a viable scenario, so that's why it's been sitting there. But now with the new the floating zone, the, you know, the mixed use opportunities, so on and so forth, I figured it I would have to go down this road to go with another plan to dissolve all of this. My biggest question is, if I were to try and retain the approval on the front commercial lots, would that then be holding me to these 19 conditions that were applied to this subdivision back in 2010? And if that's the case, then I'll just I'll just go and dissolve the whole thing and start all over again.

Okay, well I certainly am not aware of what the 19 conditions were, you know, as we were coming to talk, you know, on this tonight and I hadn't discussed the details with Jim, my thought was it probably shouldn't be a Planning and Zoning Commission item anyhow. When we normally take two lots and make them into one, that doesn't come to the Commission. But I think with the discussions that you and Agent Halsey have had, they're probably I can see that we should you know, bring an application to the Commission with, you know, what it is that you specifically want to do. I would ask you to coordinate with Jim on those 19 conditions of approval and get his input on what he thinks with respect to that. But until we have a specific here's what, you know, I would like to do from your perspective as the property owner, it's kind of tough for the Commission to weigh in on all those different issues. So I would hope that it's some future meeting. July might be, I don't know if that's doable for you. I'm not sure that it will be doable for us. I think the July meeting is going to end up being kind of full, but if you're ready, we'll try to

squeeze that in there to get at least a brief from you on on what you want to do and figure out the way ahead. But you know, certainly. I don't think it needs a public hearing to undo a subdivision, but. And I will be talking with Jim and we'll we'll talk to attorney Mark Grants on that as well in the interim to make sure that we're headed in the right direction. If you had any further interest, I know somebody came to the Commission several months ago about potentially putting a winery in on that property. Is there still an interest on that or is he I think he was abducted by aliens.

Okay. So you haven't heard anything from him recently? I'm not. That's I don't even consider that a viable alternative anymore. He just kinda just disappeared, which is pretty much par for the course in this. Yep. Nope. I agree with your goal that

probably now having a bigger piece of property with all the different options that are out there that we didn't have ten, fifteen years ago, that might be a better option. I'm sure Eric is the town administrator, doesn't look forward to losing the tax revenue that brings us, But I can see why you would want to go that route, and I think that does give the town some better flexibility to actually get the get the property developed.

Yeah, and with the with the new regulations now I can put a regular subdivision in there that has a road and has a lots and, you know, it doesn't have to be seven, eight, nine acres. It's acre and a half, now. So, I mean, it just opens up the possibility to present something. And again, like Jim mentioned earlier, I want to see what would do you guys have any suggestions for what the town would like to see there? Are you open to affordable housing? Are you open to, you know, what what is there anything that you can throw at me that that gives me some idea of what would be relatable to the town?

Well, I'll speak from the affordable housing thing. I am interested in seeing where we can find a spot to come up with a place to actually get some affordable housing in Andover. So I don't think anybody would be opposed to that. I think that'd be a great idea.

I mean, ideal scenario would be get something in there that everybody wants and then be able to use that front four or five acres and just put like a little strip mall with Starbucks or a grocer or something along those lines. And that's about the limit of really what I've looked at to this point. Unfortunately, with the rising costs in the last eighteen months of anything to do with building, Affordable housing numbers are are not what everybody thinks they are anymore.
I understand. Yep. And we'll see we'll see how all that plays out, but I understand what you're trying to do, and I think it has merit. Okay. Thank you.
Good. For clarification, you indicated you were looking for an application. We we have no application for what he's proposing to do. I mean, we could use a modification to the subdivision. I
mean, just need to have, know, our job as a commission is to take a look at what an applicant wants to do and Yep. So I think a narrative would be of a plan.

A narrative and a state plan. Yep. Yep. Okay. It specifically it should address the, you know, the previously designated open space area and the conditions of approval. Anything else on that, Jim? No. Okay.
Else, mister Cabaldi, before we go on to the next item? No. Thank you for your time, and I'll try to get something to you next month to get moving on this. Okay. Thank you. The
next next item is opting out of Public Act twenty twenty one dash 29 for the accessory dwelling units. And Abby, if you can allow me to share my screen. Okay, you should be able to.

Okay, so anyhow, one of the actions in our affordable housing plan was to opt out of accessory dwelling unit requirements that were specified in Public Act 2,129. And so, you know, why do we want to opt out? I think you probably all remember discussion in there that talked about if we allow those requirements to supersede our regulations, every property owner with a building lot would be allowed as of right to put an accessory dwelling unit on any lot that contains a single family dwelling. And, you know, I'm not sure if most towns have zoning regulations right now that discuss the accessory apartments or accessory dwelling units, but Andover does, and I think they're pretty good. I think there's a couple of things in the state recommendations that we could do, but there's an awful lot of very small lots on Andover Lake, and we're interested in trying to maintain the quality of the lake. So, you know, moving on here, our current regulations say that if you're in the Lake District and you've got a lot greater than three acres, you can put an accessory dwelling unit on that property. Andover has several very small building lots in Lake District

in and so allowing those on those very small lots would not be conducive to maintaining the water quality. So we get into the the process to opt out in, and this is the process that I would like to start tonight. The first on the list, it says that planning and zoning commission by a two thirds vote votes to initiate the opt out process. So that's all that we've got to do is I will make a motion when we get to the end here that we initiate the opt out process and we'll see if we can get, you know, a two thirds majority to vote on that. The other thing that I'd like to talk about tonight is that the opt out process requires that we hold a public hearing on this. And as we mentioned a few minutes ago, we've got a public hearing coming up prior to the July meeting to talk about a couple of our regulation changes. And I would like to include this in that public hearing as well. It just no reason not to. I don't think it's going to be a very long discussion. And so, know, when we get as part of that motion, I'll recommend that we hold a public hearing in July. Then it just talks about some of the admin, you know, if

we decide to opt out within that sixty five days after closing of the hearing, we must state on the record the reason for the decision, which is what we've been talking about. The small lots on the lake. We'll publish a notice of the decision like we do for all the decisions that we make here. And then we'll take that to the Board of Selectmen for their ratification. And I talked to Eric about this a little bit. The legislative body for Andover is a town meeting and it says here the Board of Selectmen if the town meeting is the legislative body. So I think the Board of Selectmen can ratify that, but Eric was talking to the town attorney just to make sure that we do that properly. If we don't complete the opt out process by the January 1, all those regulations, Public Act two thousand one twenty nine,

go into effect regardless of our regulations. And so, this point, you know, while I did say I think there's some things in there we might want to consider, I don't want to get into those discussions right now. We've got enough on our plate. All I want to do is opt out of them, make sure that's done before we get to the end of the year so that we can go on our business and modify the regulations in due course. But as of right now, we've got a good set of regulations that are doing as well. We may want to tweak on it just a little bit, but they are certainly very good, better than most. So with that in mind, I will make a motion to initiate the opt out process for the accessory dwelling unit regulations per Public Act 20 one-twenty nine. And in the same motion, schedule a public hearing on the opt out process for the public hearing scheduled prior to our July meeting. I'll second that. Thank you, Scott. Any discussion on that motion?

This is Leanne. I have a question just to be clear. Go ahead, Leanne. This is mainly to allow for not having this happen on small lots at the lake and then also somewhat secondarily so that people, even with larger lots, don't build the accessory units without us knowing what they're putting in?

Well, the second part of that, you know, right now, our regulations require that anybody who has a accessory apartment, accessory dwelling unit attached to their house has to come to the planning and zoning Commission with a site plan, and we can approve that. Our regulations also require right now that if somebody wants to build a detached accessory dwelling unit, for instance, the well, it could be a standalone accessory apartment or it could be in the upstairs of a barn or a garage that's detached from the house. They need to come in with a special permit. We have to have a public hearing and go through all of that. So, we currently have the facilities in place that anybody wanting to create an accessory dwelling unit, we should know about it. That will come before the Commission. So, that won't change. But the primary rationale in our affordable housing plan is to avoid giving every homeowner the right to put an accessory dwelling unit on their property regardless of the size in the Lake District. Okay, that's exactly what I asked. Thank you.

I would also add Leanne that one of the changes to the that the state is recommending in the public act would be to eliminate the requirement to have a public hearing and a special permit for a detached accessory dwelling unit. That's got some merit to it. We'll discuss that later on, our procedures are perfectly adequate, might be a little more cumbersome than someone might like, but they're good for now. The other thing we have to come through is how do we entice those people to do a ten year deed restriction so we can take credit for affordable housing on an accessory dwelling unit. But anyhow. Okay, so the last thing you mentioned is a separate item. It's not involved in this motion, right? Right. Only thing that we're going to do right now is opt out to make sure that all of those regulations that I sent you out for review do not go into effect on the January 1.
Okay.
Okay. So, for this, any other discussion? Hearing none, I'll call a roll call vote on the motion. Anne Cremay? Aye. Scott? Aye. Steve?

Aye. Leigh Ann? Aye. And I vote aye as well that motion passes five -zero-zero. To opt out of the public act requirements and to hold the public hearing in July. Okay, moving on to the next item, and this is referral under Article eight twenty four of the Connecticut General Statutes Improvement of the Property of the Town of Andover located at 15 Center Street. And Eric, it's all yours.

Okay, folks. Thank you for entertaining this. As you know, the Board of Selectmen is required to refer things to the Planning and Zoning Commission anytime they're planning on doing something that could be classified as a, you know municipal improvement and what we're talking about does qualify for that. I'm going to see whether I can share my screen here. You should see a PDF that shows Center Street and the existing, what has been referred to by many things, but it's it was for a long time the old firehouse. And then after it was the old firehouse, it was in use as a senior center and meeting center. As many of you recall, this was about five years ago, four years ago, the Board of Selectmen made a decision to discontinue using this extremely high molts and the building was getting making a lot of people very sick or uncomfortable, myself included. So, it has been in use since simply for parking of senior transportation vehicles. What the town would like to do is apply for a

grant from the state of Connecticut to tear down the existing building that is there and replace it with the parking garage that is in keeping with the character of the neighborhood and preserves the upper flat portion of the lot for other possibilities. So I'm going to stop this share and then go to what were bring up a document. Hang on a second. Okay, so the so on behalf of the board of selectmen, I am making an 08/24 statutory referral to the Planning and Zoning Commission for municipal improvement at 15 Center Street. And as a lot of you probably know, this is a building that has undergone, you know, at least three expansions since it was originally built. There are portions of this building, you know, that go back until right around 1800, But there were modifications in 1800 in like the 1890s, again around 1938 by the fire department, and then twice more by the fire department as they expanded the capacity to more and more bays. So, the structure there does not comply with current zoning because it doesn't have the required front or side yard setbacks.
So, it's close in front yard setback but it's definitely non compliant inside yard setback. The goal is to build those footprint right there is about Can you say your last sentence again?

I said the goal is to build back a smaller structure than what is there now. Currently what's there is around 50 by 71 feet, 49 by 71 feet depending on exactly where you measure it because it's not square. And the goal will be to build back a 36 foot deep by approximately 60 foot wide parking structure. So, this is a residential area and it is not going to be possible to hide the fact that this is a garage, but there's a couple different possibilities to make it blend in. The first thing is that the entire neighborhood doesn't have any real theme. There are a couple of capes, a bunch of colonials, a bunch of buildings with no apparent theme whatsoever, a couple of buildings with hip roofs.

So there's nothing aesthetically there that we can consistently match either in color or in facade look or anything. Given that the location to the railroad, the only thing I could think of would be to put a building back in there that looks like kind of a traditional parent house. And that's probably as close to matching anything as you can do there. So, I'll show you a picture of that in a second, but I just pointed out on the document that I gave you a couple of the notes in the POCD where the desire to build a structure for senior transportation or to expand senior transportation makes sense. The first is just the fact that our population is aging rapidly and the median age for residents will be over 50 years old, you know, within the next, you know, three to five years. And because of this and because of the year over year increase in need for senior transportation, we're going to need more vehicles than we have. And what we're anticipating is needing two small buses and then two smaller vehicles which is a little bit more than what we have right now. But we'll also have a vehicle where if we have to we could end up with three buses and two vehicles because of the depth of the building one of the bays could accommodate two passenger style vehicles whereas they can only hold one bus each. So, the other thing that I think is important is that if you look at the plan of conservation and development,

we note that there's very little business in industrially zoned land and it's predominantly residential. And the reason this is important is that a garage of this type would typically go in a commercial or a business zone area, but given this relative size of our business zone and our industrial zone, I think it's more likely that it's going to end up being in our residential zone somewhere. So, we've also taken a really hard look at all the town properties that we could potentially put a garage on and the public works director and myself Jay drove around and you know basically put boots on the ground on each of these sites and looked and said, okay, could we do it? What are the pluses and what are the minuses? And then we brought that back and their decision was put it back right where it is now, which does two things. One gets rid of a building that's quite an eyesore. And I'll give you a look. Is, do you see that on your screen? Yep.

This is the building that is there now. It's basically a partial cape that's been extended in the back and then it's been expanded to the left of the picture twice over the years. Frankly, it's a pretty ugly building and the roof is, you know, in the process of caving it. So, it needs to be, you know, torn down anyway. And if we're going to commit to tearing it down, we might as well reuse that same site. So, that's basically the plan. What we're looking at doing is something like you should see a picture of a white carriage house, something that matches that rough aesthetics. It's not going look exactly like that because remember it's going to be partially built into the hillside but something that looks semi historic in character along with the other houses in there. And that is basically what the town is trying to do and so it's back before you guys for an 08/24 referral and I'd be happy to answer any questions.
Does any of the commission members have, you know, questions of Eric at this point?

Yeah, Eric, do you know how much the setbacks will you said the setbacks will be improved, but it will still violate the regs. Do you know what the actual infringement will be on the required setback?

I don't know. Measuring it the other day, it looks like the building's actually set back around 43 feet now. So, I'm guessing we're going to be set back at least another two feet farther than where we are, but I don't think we can go the whole seven feet back. Because part of what we're trying to do is not pull the whole building forward, but not put it all the way back to where the existing exterior wall is. And that allows slope down to the building and reduces the structural load on the back wall of the building. So, side yard setback, I don't know what it is exactly and part of that is as part of this process, we are intending to survey this because we don't have an actual survey of this property because it's been in the town's possession since long before zoning regs. We do have partial surveys of the two houses on either side, but we don't have the town has never surveyed this part. So, we'll be able to give exact setbacks you know, which will need because it will need to go to ZBA but I don't have them for this meeting. Okay, thank you.

Eric, would the plan be for, you know, the drivers to drive their private vehicles over to the garage, leave them parked someplace in the vicinity and get the bus? Is that how that's going to work? That's correct. That's what we do now. And we will do the same thing during this.
Right now the parking area in front of the garage is wider. So, we're going to end up with basically the same width. We should be able to accommodate at least a card card than the other side.
And you said that the you you said the demolition would be covered by a grant. The the funding to rebuild is that covered by a grant too?
Yeah, so the goal here is to apply for a steep grant which is small town economic assistance program grant that will fund basically 80% of the cost of the demolition and construction of the building.

Other questions from the commission? Okay, so Eric, would it accommodate your timeline be acceptable if we took a vote on this at the next meeting? Then that gives me some time to prepare a response that I think is consistent with our plan of conservation and development?

Yes, you could definitely respond at the next meeting. That would be fine. Just I wanted to give it to you as soon as I could so you had a chance to review it and if there are further questions if you bring them back to me I'd be happy to address them.
Okay. Any last questions for Eric before we close out this topic? Okay,

hearing none, Eric, if I could get you to stay on the line for the next item too, just if we need a little help understanding the procedural process, that would be helpful to me. Okay, I can certainly do that also. So,

next up is discussion on the use of local open space funds as a match for the proposed acquisition of the Ladano property located on Shawneeville Road. And at this point, I'll turn that over to you, Hank.
Thank you, and I'd like to thank the Commission for providing us the time, the Conservation Commission, the time to present at the meeting tonight. Abby, am I able to share screen?
Yep, you should be able to, but let me know if you can't. Okay, we just call up.

The Conservation Commission is recommending that the town pursue a purchase of the 162 acre Ladano trust parcel, which is located on Shoddy Mill Road, primarily through an application to the Connecticut DEP municipal open space grant program. Just recently, the the deep announced the new grants would be available with a timeline of applications due by September 30. There is, I believe, 5,000,000 in the 2022 state budget for open space purchases and 5,000,000 in the state's open space purchases for 2023. This is something they've been doing pretty regularly throughout the years. This so this would require a match from our open space funding that we have in town, which when I last checked, which is a while ago was somewhere north of $230,000 If I recall.
